title: Ops-to-Dev Handoff: Workshop Agenda + Slide Outline + Facilitator Notes
content:
Purpose:
Run a focused ~90-minute working session to transfer operational knowledge from the internal Solutions Engineering POC team to the customer engineering and ops teams and Redwood SRE/Platform so the PoC can smoothly transition to sustained evaluation or pilot. The goal is to leave with a concrete handoff checklist, runbook draft, and assigned owners.

Audience:
- Customer engineering leads (2–4)
- Customer platform/SRE (1–2)
- Redwood Solutions Engineering (SE) lead (1)
- Redwood SRE or Platform engineer (1)
- Product/PO (optional)

Desired outcomes (what we must leave with):
1) Deployment readiness checklist with owners and dates.
2) Draft runbook for common failure modes (latency spikes, OOM, model fallback).
3) Clear network/security requirements documented and validated.
4) Agreed SLA targets for test/pilot phase and rollback policy.
5) Next-step plan (timeline, gating criteria, handover owner).

Logistics / pre-work (send 1 week before):
- Access: verify customer has sandbox VPC peering or test cluster credentials; collect IPs/CIDR.
- Dataset: customer provides sample traffic profile (CSV or synthetic generator parameters).
- Roles: ask attendees to confirm who will own monitoring and who will own deployment automation.
- Materials: share the lightweight slide deck and runbook template (this deck).

90-minute agenda (timeboxed):
- 00:00–00:05 Welcome, goals, success criteria (Facilitator - quick intros).
- 00:05–00:20 POC recap & architecture walkthrough (SE lead) — short, schematic diagram + traffic patterns.
- 00:20–00:35 Deployment constraints & networking (Customer SRE + Redwood SRE) — security rules, ingress/egress, certs, egress to telemetry.
- 00:35–00:50 Ops runbook draft walkthrough (Facilitator) — failure modes, detection, mitigation. Live edits.
- 00:50–01:05 Observability & alerting mapping (Redwood SRE) — dashboards, SLI ideas, alert thresholds.
- 01:05–01:20 Cutover/rollback plan & SLA negotiation (All) — agree on pilot window and acceptance gates.
- 01:20–01:30 Action items, owners, and follow-up timeline (Facilitator + scribe).

Slide deck outline (minimal slide titles + speaker notes bullets):
1) Title / session context
   - Who, when, why (minutes)
   - Success criteria we will measure at end
2) POC summary (1 slide)
   - Model(s) in use, inference pattern (sync/async/streaming)
   - Typical input sizes and qps observed in test
3) Architecture diagram (1 slide)
   - Components: client, gateway, inference pool, KV cache, telemetry pipeline
   - Network ports and critical paths called out
4) Deployment matrix & constraints (1 slide)
   - Regions, instance types, GPU counts, burst policies
   - Secrets/KMS, service accounts, VPC peering notes
5) Known issues & mitigations (1 slide)
   - OOM, cold-start latency, tokenization mismatches, degraded quality cases
6) Runbook skeleton (2 slides)
   - Detection -> Triage -> Mitigation -> Postmortem steps
   - Example playbook for latency spike (step-by-step)
7) Observability & Alerts (1 slide)
   - Required metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, queue length)
   - Suggested alert thresholds and escalation path
8) Cutover and rollback flow (1 slide)
   - Canary steps, traffic ramp percentages, safety gate checks
9) Action log & owners (1 slide)
   - Short-term tasks, expected dates, owners
10) Appendix: troubleshooting commands & links (1–2 slides)
   - curl examples, kubectl snippets, query templates for traces/metrics

Facilitator notes (practical guidance):
- Timebox rigorously — call out next topic 2 minutes before switch.
- Keep the architecture diagram at 1:30 scale; don’t get pulled into implementation details. If a deep dive is needed, capture as follow-up ticket.
- Live-edit the runbook in a shared Google Doc; the scribe should capture exact wording for ownership lines.
- Use probing questions to align expectations early: e.g., "What is the maximum acceptable 95th percentile latency for user-facing calls?" "Who is first-on-call during the pilot?"
- If customers request feature work (SDK changes, model changes) during session, mark as separate product/engineering request and do not let it derail operations negotiation.

Runbook draft (copyable bullets for the Google Doc):
- Detection: metrics to watch (p95 latency > X ms, GPU util > 90%, queue length > 50)
- Triage: check logs -> correlate request ids -> verify model process health -> check QC cache hit rate
- Mitigation: scale up pool (manual or autoscale hint), shift traffic to fallback model, flush KV cache, restart stuck workers with circuit-breaker window
- Postmortem: timeline, root cause, action owners, regression test to add to Redwood Optimize

Observability quick checklist (things to wire before pilot):
- Export token-level cost breakdown to billing dashboard
- Application traces include model_id and request_id
- Dashboard widgets for per-host GPU memory and per-queue latency
- Alert for telemetry pipeline lag > 2 minutes

Roles and responsibilities (short):
- Customer platform lead: VPC, firewall rules, certs, hosting account config
- Customer SRE: on-call for pilot, alert tuning, runbook owner (if agreed)
- Redwood SE: POC knowledge transfer, runbook co-author, remediation assistance in pilot window
- Redwood SRE: production-hardening recommendations, dashboard templates, escalation contact

Common risks and mitigations (fast list):
- Risk: Missing network rules delay test traffic —> Mitigation: pre-check firewall rules + test connectivity step in pre-work.
- Risk: Observability not instrumented —> Mitigation: provide minimal instrumentation snippet and short integration script during session.
- Risk: Model drift between POC dataset and pilot traffic —> Mitigation: reserve short regression test and data sampling during pilot ramp.

Post-work deliverables and timeline (example):
- 48 hours: runbook v0 exported and assigned (owner: Customer SRE + Redwood SE).
- 5 business days: dashboard and alerts in place with one test alert executed (owner: Redwood SRE).
- 10 business days: pilot cutover checklist completed and pilot start date scheduled.

Follow-up / communications templates (send within 24h):
- Short summary email with 3 bullets: what we agreed, immediate blockers, next meeting slot.
- Shared Google Doc link (runbook) and slide deck export.
- JIRA epic created for pilot with acceptance criteria and owners.

Quick facilitation script (first 5 minutes):
1) Welcome + 30s purpose.
2) "Go-around" intros: name, role, what success looks like for you today (15s each).
3) Confirm success criteria slide and ask for additions.

Notes to scribe (what to capture):
- Exact toggles/flags needed for cutover.
- IP/CIDR and service account names.
- Any deviations from the POC architecture agreed in meeting.

Parking lot (for later):
- API schema changes request from customer product team.
- Perf regression suspected in tokenizer; needs perf test ticket.

Acceptance criteria for handoff completion:
- Runbook v0 approved by customer SRE and Redwood SE.
- Monitoring coverage (key metrics + one alert test) validated.
- Pilot start window scheduled and owners assigned.

Checklist for session facilitator (day of):
- Slides loaded and shared doc ready, scribe assigned, recording enabled.
- Connectivity test to customer sandbox done 24h prior.
- Pre-populate runbook with known items so edits are quick.

Appendix: example trouble commands (copy into appendix slide)
- curl -H 'x-request-id: test123' https://api.example.test/v1/generate -v
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-inference -o wide
- query for traces: service.name:inference AND trace.duration > 1000ms

End of doc.
